title: At Velvet Static, the opening DJ drops a perfect mashup. You filmed it. The DJ has 41 followers.

options.label: Post it and tag the DJ
options.get: Clout, and a DJ who loves you
options.riskWhy: Credit is hard to get wrong

outcomes.text: Mags gives you the DJ's handle and an approving pour. The DJ goes from 41 followers to 900 overnight.

later.text: Remember tagging the opening DJ at Velvet Static? She's headlining now, and she put you on her list for life. Mags poured you one on the house.

outcomes.text: 'Cooked this one up 🔥.' You did not cook it. You don't own headphones. People think you're a DJ now.

later.text: Remember posting the Velvet Static mashup as your set? The real DJ posted the project file with a timestamp. Mags waters your drinks now.

outcomes.text: You put the phone away and dance like nobody's filming. Somebody is. You look great.

title: Rain, a 90-minute line at The Kiln, and Rocco the bouncer just recognized you from the 7 train.

outcomes.text: You wave at Rocco and stay in line. He nods: respect. Your hair does not survive the 90 minutes.
Rocco unhooks the rope. You walk past eighty wet strangers like a minor celebrity. The music is better dry.
Rocco unhooks the rope. The line boos with real commitment. Someone posts 'who is THAT' and it isn't flattering.
You share your umbrella with the woman behind you. She's a talent booker. You talk for 90 minutes. You're both soaked.

later.text: Remember sharing your umbrella in The Kiln's line? The booker put you on the list for a private show. The rope opened by itself.

title: You're on Kiki's rooftop list, no plus-one. A stranger in line offers C$60 to be your 'cousin.'

outcomes.text: 'Sorry, no cousins.' Kiki checks you in with a grin. She heard. She hears everything at the rope.
'This is my cousin.' Kiki looks at you, then at him, then at you. She lets you both in. C$60 richer.

later.text: Remember your C$60 'cousin' at the rooftop? He told Kiki how he got in. She's taken you off the list for a week. 'Family business,' she says.

options.label: Ask Kiki if he can come

outcomes.text: 'Kiki, he's not my cousin, but he's nice.' She laughs. 'Honest. Fine. He pays the door.' He does. You don't take his C$60.
'He's not my cousin, but can he come?' Kiki: 'No, but thanks for not lying.' He leaves. She saves you the best heat lamp.

title: At Low Light Lounge, a man whispers: 'Tell Marcos I'm with you. I'm a talent scout. I'll owe you.'

options.label: 'Sorry, can't'
options.cost: Whatever a scout's favor is worth

outcomes.text: You shake your head. Marcos, polishing a glass, gives you the smallest nod. In this lounge, that's a key.

options.label: 'He's with me'
options.cost: Vouching for a stranger to Marcos
options.riskWhy: Marcos keeps a list of who vouched

outcomes.text: 'He's with me.' Marcos lets him through. The scout winks and disappears into the back room.

later.text: Remember vouching for the 'talent scout' at Low Light? He was a tabloid photographer. Marcos lost a regular. He hasn't said a word to you since.

outcomes.text: 'Marcos, this guy says he's a scout. I just met him.' Marcos asks two questions and shows him the door, politely. He buys you a drink.

title: In Low Light's back room, you hear Lunaria's 3 AM 'surprise' album is delayed a year. Lola pays well.

options.label: Keep it in the back room

outcomes.text: Marcos says it to everyone once: what's said in the back room stays there. You nod. It stays.

later.text: Remember keeping Lunaria's album news to yourself? Marcos noticed. He let you sit in on her secret listening session. Phones in the box.

options.label: Sell it to Lola
options.riskWhy: Only six people were in that room

outcomes.text: Lola runs it as BREAKING: 'Lunaria's album? Delayed, babe.' C$200. Lunaria's fans are spiraling. So is Marcos.

later.text: Remember selling Lunaria's album news to Lola? Marcos worked out who was in the back room. There were six. You're no longer one of them.

outcomes.text: 'Don't hold your breath for 3 AM, Lunaria fans.' Mystery clout. Marcos reads it and frowns, but can't prove a thing.

title: A promoter at The Sticky Floor: 'Heard you're flexible. C$250 to tell your followers Dunk Daniels is coming.'

outcomes.text: 'Nah.' The promoter looks surprised. Your reputation had suggested otherwise. You surprise yourself a little too.
'Dunk Daniels at The Sticky Floor tonight, trust me 🏀.' 300 people come. Dunk is late to everything, so it holds an hour.

later.text: Remember telling everyone Dunk Daniels would be at The Sticky Floor? He wasn't. 300 people know whose post it was. The comments are not kind.

options.label: Post 'rumor has it'
options.cost: A little of your followers' trust

outcomes.text: 'Rumor has it someone tall is at The Sticky Floor 👀.' Half the crowd, half the pay. Someone tall shows up. It's a regular named Kevin.

title: Discount Disco's owner: C$200 to post a teary 'this night changed my life' video. You've never been.

outcomes.text: 'Pass.' The owner offers C$250. 'Still pass.' He's genuinely confused. So is your reputation.
You think about your rent and cry beautifully. 'This place healed me.' C$200. The video does numbers.

later.text: Remember the teary Discount Disco video? Someone found four other people saying the same words, in the same shirt. Lola ran them side by side.

options.label: Go first, then post the truth
options.riskWhy: He paid for tears, not truth

outcomes.text: You go. It's fine. The DJ plays one song twice. You post 'honestly decent, C$5 drinks.' The owner pays half, grumbling.
You go and actually have a great night. Your honest post is glowing. The owner pays in full and looks confused.
